title: The Faithful Betrayal
text:
Literary translation is often described as an act of faithful betrayal. The translator must render the sense of a text while accepting that certain nuances, rhythms, and cultural allusions will inevitably be lost in the process. A rendering that is technically accurate may nonetheless feel lifeless, whereas a bolder version can capture the spirit of the original at the cost of literal fidelity.

Consider the translation of wordplay, which resists direct transfer. A pun that delights readers in one language may have no equivalent in another, forcing the translator to invent a new joke that serves the same narrative function. Such decisions reveal how much of a translator's craft lies not in substitution but in judgment.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must the translator accept?
options: That some nuances and cultural allusions will be lost
That rhythm can always be preserved
That readers will never notice any changes

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say about puns?
options: They translate easily into any language
They may have no equivalent in another language
They are rarely used in literature

questions.text: What does the author imply about a translation that is technically accurate but lifeless?
options: It is usually preferred by critics
It may fail to convey the spirit of the original
It is more faithful than a bolder version

questions.text: Which conclusion do the final sentences of the passage most strongly support?
options: Translation is mainly a mechanical process
Translators make judgment-based decisions beyond word substitution
Wordplay should be avoided in translation
Literal translation is the only ethical approach

paragraph_translations: La traduccion literaria suele describirse como un acto de traicion fiel. El traductor debe transmitir el sentido de un texto aceptando que ciertos matices, ritmos y alusiones culturales se perderan inevitablemente en el proceso. Una version tecnicamente precisa puede resultar, sin embargo, sin vida, mientras que una version mas audaz puede captar el espiritu del original a costa de la fidelidad literal.

Consideremos la traduccion de los juegos de palabras, que se resisten a la transferencia directa. Un juego de palabras que deleita a los lectores en una lengua puede no tener equivalente en otra, lo que obliga al traductor a inventar un nuevo chiste que cumpla la misma funcion narrativa. Decisiones como estas revelan que gran parte del oficio del traductor reside no en la sustitucion, sino en el juicio.
